the long-term effects of a maternal low-protein diet on mitochondrial changes in the pancreatic islets of offspring and whether taurin supplementation to this diet can restore these mitochondrial changes.

taurine supplementation during pregnancy and lactating period can prevent the mitochondrial changes caused by protein malnutrition in the fetal period and thus can prevent the development of type-2 diabetes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maternal protein malnutrition during pregnancy leads to mitochondrial dysfunction in pancreatic islets of the offspring, which may be a link between fetal undernutrition and adult type 2 diabetes.

taurine supplementation during pregnancy and lactational periods may prevent the development of type-2 diabetes later in the life of offspring of rats fed with protein-restriction diet during the gestation.

maternal taurine deficiency may play a role in the mitochondrial dysfunction of pancreatic islet cells, which may contribute to the later development of diabetes in the offspring of malnourished mothers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
taurine supplementation during pregnancy and lactations can prevent the long-term adverse effects of protein restriction in pregnancy.
taurine supplementation to a low-protein maternal diet can restore these changes and prevent the development of type-2 diabetes later in adulthood.
